rationale: Lycopolitan form of ⲟⲩϣⲏ 'night' (feminine). Forms the structural counterpart to ⲍⲟⲟⲩⲉ 'days' in the cosmological scheme of Four Days (light) / Four Nights (darkness). The first three Nights identified on this page are: (1) Land of Darkness, (2) Matter / hyle, (3) the five worlds of flesh.

Greek loanword ζωγράφος 'painter of living things, image-maker.' Used here as a cosmological epithet of Matter (hyle): she is the principle who paints/depicts forms onto the dark substrate, fashioning the archontic order. The verbal form ⲍⲱⲣⲡⲁⲫⲉ in line 12 confirms (= ζωγραφεῖν 'to paint, depict').
Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ 'shadow.' Used here for the Twelve Shadows of darkness — the dark counterparts to the Twelve Aeons of light. Each Night has its twelve shadows.
Variant spelling of ⲕⲙⲏⲙⲉ 'darkness, blackness.' Used attributively here ('shadows of darkness').
Lycopolitan ⲍⲙⲁⲙ = Sahidic ϩⲙⲟⲙ 'heat, warmth.' Paired with ⲁⲣⲁϣ 'cold' as cosmic-elemental dyad.
Lycopolitan ⲁⲣⲁϣ = Sahidic ⲱⲣϣ̄ 'cold.' Pair-partner with ⲍⲙⲁⲙ 'heat.'

Greek loanword ἡδονή 'pleasure, sensual delight.' Used here as the maternal cosmic principle (paired with ⲥⲉⲧⲉ 'fire' = paternal). Standard Manichaean negative valuation of bodily/sensual desire as cosmic principle.
Lycopolitan ⲗⲁϩ = strife, fight, struggle. Forms standing pair with ⲡⲡⲟⲗⲉⲙⲟⲥ 'the war' for the cosmic primordial battle.

proposed_english: to be bound upon / fettered upon
rationale: Verb of binding/fettering with directional ⲁⲣⲁ⸗ 'upon (her/him).' The dark powers are 'bound upon' the First Man / upon Matter — describing the Manichaean cosmological capture of evil powers.
Lycopolitan ⲥⲁⲛⲧⲧⲉ = ⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ 'side of heaven, upper region.' Variant of the well-attested ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ in the accumulated vocabulary.
Lycopolitan ⲥⲁ-ⲙ-ⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ / ⲥⲁⲛⲧⲓⲧⲛⲉ = 'side of below.' Spatial pair-partner with ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ 'the upper side.'
Verb of mingling/intermixing. Used here of how the elements mingle 'into one another' (ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ ⲁⲛⲟⲩⲉⲣⲏⲩ) within the cosmic structure of Matter.
Verb describing the defeat of the dark powers by the First Man. Likely Lycopolitan reflex of a verb of striking/falling. Tentative.
